grammar_focus: Review SD50-71 复习难点(教材 L72 Special difficulties):经常容易混淆的词——lose/miss、expect/wait、raise/rise、lie/lay、beat/win、value/cost/price、accept/agree、say/tell、dress up、hung(悬挂)、hard/hardly、near/nearly;辅以课文语法过去完成被动(had been specially built / a mistake had been made)与现在完成(have reached)
scene: 杰出的赛车手马尔科姆·坎贝尔爵士是第一个以每小时超过300英里的速度驾车的人。他于1935年9月在犹他州的邦纳维尔盐滩创造了一项新的世界纪录。他驾驶的“蓝鸟”牌汽车是专门为他制造的。车身长30多英尺,装有一台2500马力的发动机。尽管坎贝尔达到了每小时超过304英里的速度,但因为开始那圈爆了一只轮胎,他很难控制住汽车。比赛结束后,坎贝尔失望地得知他的平均时速是299英里。然而几天之后,有人告诉他弄错了,他的平均时速实际是301英里。从那以后,赛车手已达到每小时600多英里的速度。很多年后,马尔科姆爵士的儿子唐纳德踏着父亲的足迹,也创造了一项世界纪录。同父亲一样,他驾驶的也是一辆叫“蓝鸟”的汽车。

grammar_card.title: Review SD50-71 易混词复习
grammar_card.intro: 本课复习前面若干课的“经常容易混淆的词”:①lose(丢失)vs miss(错过、没赶上);②expect(预计会…)vs wait(等待);③raise(抬高、举起,后面接宾语)vs rise(升起,自己升);④lie(躺,lying)vs lay(放置,laying);⑤beat sb(击败某人)vs win(赢得比赛/奖);⑥value(看重)/cost(花费多少钱)/price(定价、价格);⑦accept(接受)vs agree(同意);⑧say sth(说某话)vs tell sb(告诉某人);⑨dress up(装扮成);⑩hang→hung(悬挂物品);⑪hard(努力地)vs hardly(几乎不);⑫near(靠近)vs nearly(几乎)。另配课文语法:过去完成被动 had been done、现在完成 have done。

rows: miss=错过没赶上(miss the train);lose=丢失(lose your keys)
expect=预计会…(expecting a letter);wait=在等(waiting for a bus)
raise=抬高、举起后接宾语;rise=自己升起不接宾语
cost=花费多少钱;price=价格、定价;value=看重
hard=努力地(work hard);hardly=几乎不(hardly ever)

specialRules.rule: 美语里“练习”名词动词都拼 practice(英式动词才拼 practise);本课只教 practice 一种拼法。
hang 两套变化:表“悬挂(物品)”hang-hung-hung(She hung the washing);旧时“绞死(人)”才用 hanged(仅认读,不作重点)。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What mistake was made?
options: His average speed was first declared 299 mph, but it was really 301 mph
His car was too heavy to drive
He started the race on the wrong day

passage: The great racing driver, Sir Malcolm Campbell, was the first man to drive at over 300 miles per hour. He set up a new world record in September 1935 at Bonneville Salt Flats, Utah. Bluebird, the car he was driving, had been specially built for him. It was over 30 feet in length and had a 2,500-horsepower engine. Although Campbell reached a speed of over 304 miles per hour, he had great difficulty in controlling the car because a tire burst during the first run. After his attempt, Campbell was disappointed to learn that his average speed had been 299 miles per hour. However, a few days later, he was told that a mistake had been made. His average speed had been 301 miles per hour. Since that time, racing drivers have reached speeds over 600 miles an hour. Following in his father's footsteps many years later, Sir Malcolm's son, Donald, also set up a world record. Like his father, he was driving a car called Bluebird.
